item.name: player service
item.description: Real Player CRUD/login/teams through Gateway at localhost:8090. Run in order against the new baseline source/reviewed image, not the old pinned Lab 3 image. Player and Gateway require matching RSA private/public keys and distinct machine target credentials. Login supplies real access/refresh tokens in transient runner variables; never export populated secrets. Backend identity is bound to verified JWT sub. Synthetic accounts are deleted at the end; no internal operations or fabricated JWTs are used. Refreshed 2026-11-12 from shared dev bdf7190. Gateway boundary and separate operational log checks are included. Current private service source was not accessible during this review; public shared contracts do not establish runtime acceptance. See ../docs/lab4-configuration-review.md.

item.name: Lab 4 Task 3 - Gateway boundary
item.description: Public Gateway health, JWT and internal-route boundary checks. Run with the current Lab 4 subscriber-queue Gateway/Broker deployment.

request.description: Public Gateway relay for this service's existing health/readiness endpoint. Requires a running, healthy service and its database; this does not probe the custom broker.

exec: pm.test('Service health through Gateway: HTTP 200', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Explicit No Auth overrides the collection bearer token. Gateway must reject this request before forwarding it to the owned service.

exec: pm.test('Gateway rejects unauthorized access: HTTP 401', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

pm.test('Gateway uses the existing authentication error contract', () => { const error = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(error.code).to.eql('UNAUTHENTICATED'); pm.expect(error.service).to.eql('gateway-service'); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate')).to.eql('Bearer'); });

pm.test('Authentication error matches the response trace ID', () => { const traceId = pm.response.headers.get('X-Trace-Id'); pm.expect(traceId).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.traceId).to.eql(traceId); });

request.description: No Auth disables inherited authorization; the deliberately incomplete Bearer header contains no token. Gateway must return its existing 401 error.

pm.test('Gateway uses the existing authentication error contract', () => { const error = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(error.code).to.eql('UNAUTHENTICATED'); pm.expect(error.service).to.eql('gateway-service'); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate')).to.eql('Bearer'); });

pm.test('Authentication error matches the response trace ID', () => { const traceId = pm.response.headers.get('X-Trace-Id'); pm.expect(traceId).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.traceId).to.eql(traceId); });
pm.test('Internal route is not public', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

item.name: Gateway currently blocks logout (known route gap)

request.description: The published Gateway lab4-2.1.1 allowlist omits POST /players/logout. This asserts the current 404 boundary, not successful logout/revocation. A future Gateway release must add this user-facing route before restoring the positive 204 logout check.

exec: pm.test('Gateway rejects this method/path: HTTP 404', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));
pm.test('Gateway route boundary error', () => { const error = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(error.code).to.eql('ROUTE_NOT_FOUND'); pm.expect(error.service).to.eql('gateway-service'); });

item.name: Lab 4 Task 4 - Operational logs
item.description: Start the local log-download endpoint for the exact running Compose project. Set logDownloadUrl and a private logDownloadToken; this is a separate operations credential, not the collection's Player JWT. The download is limited to this owned service and its declared numeric replicas. To download the whole system, omit the service query on the same endpoint.

exec: pm.test('Exporter is UP', () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.service).to.eql('log-download-service'); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('UP'); });

request.description: A finite text attachment from the selected Compose project. A 503 means the local Docker/configuration source is unavailable; it is not a successful empty log export.

exec: pm.test('Owned service snapshot includes the requested bounds', () => { const text = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(text).to.include('services=player-service'); pm.expect(text).to.include('since=15m; tail=200 per container'); });

pm.test('Operations authentication error is traceable', () => { const error = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(error.code).to.eql('UNAUTHORIZED'); pm.expect(error.service).to.eql('log-download-service'); pm.expect(error.traceId).to.eql(pm.response.headers.get('X-Trace-Id')); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate')).to.eql('Bearer'); });

pm.test('Invalid query uses the operations contract', () => { const error = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(error.code).to.eql('INVALID_LOG_QUERY'); pm.expect(error.service).to.eql('log-download-service'); pm.expect(error.traceId).to.eql(pm.response.headers.get('X-Trace-Id')); });

item.name: session service
item.description: Real owned-service baseline through Gateway at localhost:8090. Run Core CRUD and access first; it creates two real Player accounts/tokens, a persistent team and a session. Tokens use transient runner variables, never tracked/exported values. Optional shift requests require receiver-approved Rules selection plus real Applicant/DMs/Moderation dependencies and manual readiness/decision steps; do not call their absence a successful full-shift test. No fixture IDs or spoofed X-Player-Id headers are used. Core leaves a session/accounts for optional follow-up; clean up only these generated IDs afterward. Refreshed 2026-11-12 from shared dev bdf7190. Gateway boundary and separate operational log checks are included. Current private service source was not accessible during this review; public shared contracts do not establish runtime acceptance. See ../docs/lab4-configuration-review.md.

item.name: moderation service
item.description:
Moderation Service (Java), reached through the Gateway on {{baseUrl}} as the communication contract requires: no request here talks to the service's own port. Lab 4: there are no mocks. Decisions are scored from the real Session, Applicant, Credential and Rules owners through the Message Broker (Lab 4: topic publications, over gRPC from Task 8; see docs/messaging-grpc.md), so this collection needs a real session ({{moderation_sessionId}}) in which the moderator, junior and outsider tokens hold those roles, and real applicants of that session whose owners generated the stated deceptions ({{moderation_applicantBanned}}, {{moderation_applicantRuleBreaker}}, {{moderation_applicantInconsistent}}, {{moderation_applicantExpiredDocument}}). Until every operation marked requested in the catalog is implemented by its owner, submit requests fail closed with 503 <DEPENDENCY>_UNAVAILABLE, which is the expected behaviour, not a pass.

Authentication: every request sends Bearer the appropriate private player token, a real access JWT of that player (Player login, or a disposable local test signer whose public key the Gateway and DMs are configured with). The Gateway verifies it and sets X-Player-Id from its subject, so this collection sends no X-Player-Id: identity cannot be chosen by the client. Keep tokens in a private Postman environment, never in tracked files. The health request uses no authentication. Penalty-policy writes use {{moderation_policyAdminToken}}, a player listed in MODERATION_POLICY_ADMINS. Lab 4 folders: Task 3 Gateway boundary, Task 4 operational logs (log-download endpoint), Tasks 5-8 Message Broker (topics, events, topic listing). HTTP topic publication tests exercise the Broker compatibility ingress; native gRPC publication uses messaging.proto. Broker-to-service gRPC delivery requires a matching transport catalog and healthy receivers.

item.description:
Discord DMs Service (Go), REST reached through the Gateway on {{baseUrl}}. Lab 4: no mocks. Every permission comes from the real Session Service through the Message Broker (session.verifyMembership, published over gRPC from Lab 4 Task 8), so {{discord_dms_sessionId}} must be a real session in which the moderator and junior tokens hold the listed channel assignments (junior 1: #enrollment-check and #general-mod-chat; junior 2: #faculty-check and #general-mod-chat), and its ShiftStarted must have been delivered to DMs through the Message Broker (event.ShiftStarted.v1) so the default channels exist. The old internal /api/v1/internal/... stand-ins are removed. WebSocket: negotiate through the Gateway with the same token and connect to the returned URL.

Authentication: every request sends Bearer the appropriate private player token, a real access JWT of that player (Player login, or a disposable local test signer whose public key the Gateway and DMs are configured with). The Gateway verifies it and sets X-Player-Id from its subject, so this collection sends no X-Player-Id: identity cannot be chosen by the client. Keep tokens in a private Postman environment, never in tracked files. The health request uses no authentication. Lab 4 folders: Task 3 Gateway boundary, Task 4 operational logs (log-download endpoint), Tasks 5-8 Message Broker (topics, events, topic listing). HTTP topic publication tests exercise the Broker compatibility ingress; native gRPC publication uses messaging.proto. Broker-to-service gRPC delivery requires a matching transport catalog and healthy receivers.
